summary.headline: Kuantum Papers Q4 FY26 EBITDA rose 22% QoQ to INR48 crore (15.90% margin) on NSR of INR3,700/MT, despite input cost pressure.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 operational income was INR301 crore, up 4% QoQ, driven by NSR improvement to INR3,700/MT, while input costs rose about INR2,000/MT amid the West Asia conflict. EBITDA reached INR48 crore (margin 15.90%, up 234 bps QoQ) and PAT INR14 crore (margin 4.75%, up 137 bps QoQ). For FY26, revenue fell 1% YoY to INR1,093 crore and EBITDA was INR162 crore (14.80% margin), with NSR down about INR2,000/MT and costs up about INR3,200/MT. Management guided to volume growth to about 2,30,000 MT and EBITDA margin of 18-20% over the next few years, with PM3 upgrade and pulp (DDS) commissioning slated for mid-June to July 2026.

segments.name: Notebook paper
segments.commentary: Share fell from about 22% of sales before the September GST change to about 7-8% now; management intends to exit the segment after machine upgrades, citing reversal of input tax credit at nil GST.

segments.name: Copier, high-end printing, specialty paper
segments.commentary: Copier share is growing steadily; Maplitho and size grades target high-end printing; specialty grades targeted at 20-30% of production volume.

segments.name: Paperboard
segments.commentary: Management noted MIP for paperboard continues with a one-year extension; paperboard was not discussed in detail.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top line expected at INR1,400-1,500 crore, rising gradually to INR1,600 crore; FY28 INR1,600-1,700 crore (management's medium-term view: INR1,600-1,700 crore).
Volumes to rise from about 1,62,000-1,63,000 MT to about 2,30,000 MT, a 40-50% increase, at utilisation above 90-95%.
EBITDA margin target of 18-20% over the medium term.
Operating cost reduction of 5-8% of total manufacturing cost once AI/digital projects are fully implemented, expected across machines by FY27-FY28.
Peak long-term debt of INR650-675 crore by end-2027, reducing INR100-200 crore a year thereafter; annual repayments of INR170-180 crore over the next 2-3 years.
Remaining capex of about INR125 crore to be spent in FY27; no new capex planned beyond current projects, though another expansion may be considered in about two years.
Tissue paper project deferred, not shelved, until debt is under control.
Wheat straw prices expected to ease after rice sowing starts in early June; Q1 season expected to be lean with pricing pressure.
capex_capacity: PM2 rebuild completed March 2026, capacity raised to 75 TPD; PM1 rebuild in December 2025 added about 20 TPD on average in Q4.
PM3 upgrade delayed due to German imported parts; now planned by mid-June/July 2026 (previously around May).
Displacement Digester System (DDS) for wood pulping under extensive testing, commissioning targeted by mid-June; pulp capacity to come on stream by PM3 commissioning (July).
Two-stage recausticizing plant and 80 TPD synchro sheeter commissioned; overall utilisation above 92% on PM1, PM2 and PM4 (OE levels).
Cost of PM3 upgrade not expected to escalate versus the earlier INR140-150 crore estimate.
demand_pricing: Pricing firmed in Q4 on higher demand, but May price hikes partly reversed; management says it holds prices at about INR69,000-70,000/ton.
Low-priced imports persisted through FY26, lowering domestic prices; West Asia freight disruption reduced import volumes in Q4, with risk of China/Indonesia trade diversion.

Anti-subsidy application expected to be processed by FY-end (March 2027); anti-dumping application on writing and printing paper typically takes 1.5-2 years; MIP for writing/printing paper still under review.
Global pulp prices at about USD600-700/ton, expected to stay in that range given new capacity additions.
Wheat straw prices up about 50-60% YoY, with the fuel-use competition now unwound; wood chip prices broadly stable.
Chemical input costs up about 3-5% for some chemicals; the company is absorbing rather than passing these through.
Dealer network of about 90 committed dealers plus about 20 irregular dealers; Gulf and North African export markets being developed.

qa_highlights.question: Are import pressures visible now, and will they hurt pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volumes from China and Indonesia did not arrive in Q4 due to West Asia freight disruption; the impact may return later, and the industry is pursuing Gulf export opportunities. Comment restricted to white paper, not paperboard.

qa_highlights.question: Current debt and capex plans for FY27-FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term debt was INR720 crore on 31 March 2026; peak debt of INR650-675 crore by end-2027. Remaining capex of about INR125 crore in FY27 and no new capex planned beyond existing projects.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of PM3 and pulp capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: PM3 delayed due to German parts, now targeted by mid-June; pulp upgrade to come on stream alongside PM3 in July 2026.

qa_highlights.question: How will the new capacity be absorbed, given the demand environment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 95%+ utilisation; cited the dealer network, Gulf and Northern Africa markets, and a 25-30% specialty grade mix as offsets.

qa_highlights.question: How much opex can be cut from AI and capacity additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 5-8% of total manufacturing cost reduction once AI systems are deployed across machines, progressing machine by machine and mill-wide, with completion targeted by FY27-FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company refinance or reduce cost of funds?
qa_highlights.answer: Average long-term cost of funds is about 8.5%; management is exploring FCNRB and cheaper funding options. Buybacks are not being considered for now.

risks_watch: Import pressure from China and Indonesia, and dumping, could return once freight normalises; the anti-subsidy outcome is a key dependency.
Ramp-up risk: volumes must rise 40-50% to about 2,30,000 MT, with pulp capacity and PM3 timelines already slipping.
Leverage is high: long-term debt of INR720 crore at about 8.5% average cost, with annual repayments of INR170-180 crore.
Lean season expected in the next 2-3 months with historical pricing dips; management expects reversal around September.
Input costs (chemicals, wheat straw, pulp) remain elevated; the company is absorbing chemical cost increases.
Notebook exit reduces the top line and may affect volume in the near term.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operating momentum and medium-term targets, but cautious on near-term pricing and input costs; several answers were corrective or deferred, including the tissue project and the MIP and ADD outcomes. Management was defensive when challenged on capacity absorption and debt.
key_quotes: Encouragingly, pricing began to fir m up in the fourth quarter, supported by higher demand, though was dampened a bit by the cost-led adjustments due to the ongoing West Asia conflict.
So, you can expect the top line to be in the range of INR1,600 crores to INR1,700 crores thereabouts.
And we are not foreseeing any kind of stiff competition, particularly for us.
It's a conscious call not to remain in this segment.

adds.what: PM3 machine upgrade (delayed on German imported parts; now planned mid-June/July 2026)
Displacement Digester System (DDS) wood pulping; commissioning targeted mid-June, pulp capacity on stream with PM3

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue of INR1,400-1,500 crore (about 31% over FY26's INR1,093 crore midpoint) and volumes to about 2,30,000 MT (40-50% up), backed by PM3 upgrade and DDS pulp commissioning slated mid-June to July 2026, but PM3 has already slipped and no firm order book is cited.
